outcome: Human editing now uses a durable Working copy instead of creating a revision on every save
owner_impact: While editing an owned Experiment, leaving an editor or taking another action autosaves the current text into one unnumbered Working copy. Save Revision is the only human action that crystallizes it into the next numbered revision. Numbered snapshots are retained immutably, incomplete edits can still autosave, and a newer AI revision no longer invalidates or blocks the human Working copy.

next.text: #396 continues with #398 — revision selector, Working copy navigation, and All/Mine/AI filters. That ticket will make retained history and newly arrived AI revisions directly visible/selectable and will holistically redesign the touched Experiment/revision UI. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Production migrations 20260920094310 and 20260920094339 add immutable experiment_revisions, owner-only experiment_working_copies, RLS, retained-base provenance, and the explicit crystallization RPC.
Existing Experiment rows were backfilled only at their current stored revision; overwritten historical contents were not fabricated.
The existing AI Experiment write path remains compatible and automatically appends numbered snapshots through the database trigger; the research-AI connector contract did not change.
Human Working-copy persistence accepts temporarily incomplete scientific text, while Save Revision retains the runnable Experiment validation boundary.
Collection-only moves no longer manufacture scientific revision numbers or overwrite revision provenance.
No CI/CD, deployment, polling, retry, timeout, scheduling, connector-tool surface, or project-workflow rule changed.
